Adhunika Chitti

Business Analytics Professional · Data-Driven Storyteller

I'm a Business Analytics graduate of Northern Arizona University, turning messy, real-world data into decisions people can act on. Over the past year I've cleaned and modeled 1.58 million+ transit ridership records for the City of Flagstaff, built predictive models in Python and RapidMiner, and translated results into plain-language recommendations for non-technical stakeholders. I care as much about the story behind the numbers as the numbers themselves — dashboards, presentations, and reports that make people confident enough to act. Alongside the analytics, I've built fluency in AI-assisted workflows: prompt engineering, LLM auditing, and directing AI tools through structured, defensible analysis. I'm now looking for a full-time role where I can bring that same rigor — clean data, clear models, honest storytelling — to a team that needs it. Let's talk about what I could build for you.

About Me

The analyst behind the dashboard

I recently graduated with my MS in Business Analytics from Northern Arizona University (3.8 GPA), building on a Bachelor of Business Administration from VIT-AP University, where I graduated 6th in my class with an 8.93 CGPA. My toolkit spans Python (pandas, scikit-learn), SQL, RapidMiner, Tableau, and Power BI, and I've used all of it on real client work — most recently an end-to-end ridership analysis for Mountain Line, Flagstaff's public transit agency. What I bring beyond the technical skills is translation: time spent working directly with non-technical stakeholders, from a support role at NAU ITS to client-facing capstone presentations, taught me how to explain a model without losing the person across the table. I've also put real time into AI and prompt engineering coursework — few-shot prompting, chain-of-thought reasoning, and auditing LLM outputs for inflated claims — because I think analysts fluent in both statistics and AI tooling will do the most useful work over the next decade. Outside coursework, I've presented original research at an international conference, mentored high school scholars in a college-access program, and led documentation for a busy student business club. What ties it together is a preference for evidence over instinct, and for explaining the "why" clearly enough that someone else can act on it. I'm now looking for a full-time analytics role where I can put all of this to work.

Mission

To turn overlooked data into decisions that improve real systems — transit routes, customer experience, business operations — for people who don't have time to read a regression output.

Vision

To become an analyst whose reports get acted on, not filed away — someone teams trust to tell them the truth the data is showing, even when it's inconvenient.
